analyst.summary: Balrampur Chini Mills, India's largest integrated sugar-and-ethanol producer, grew FY26 standalone revenue 15.8% on higher cane crushing, but consolidated profit was roughly flat-to-down (EPS fell to Rs.18.74 from Rs.21.65) as rising cane costs met government ethanol prices that have not moved in three years, while the company also builds a large new Rs.3,080 crore bioplastics (PLA) plant due on stream late 2026. The stock trades at a rich ~32x trailing earnings for a business with ~11-12% returns on capital, so the multiple is really a bet on the new bioplastics business paying off - we are holding the position but flagging the earnings-quality gap for closer review rather than adding.
